title: How SAP Store Certification Turns into Customer Trust for Vertex
summary: Vertex embeds tax calculation natively into SAP order-to-cash flows. Learn how SAP Store can shorten the trust-building work with customers.
body_markdown:
Tax is one of those business functions nobody wants to think about until something goes wrong. Vertex, one of the largest[indirect tax software](https://sap.com/products/financial-management/tax-and-trade-management.html) companies in the world, has spent more than two decades making sure that for SAP customers, nothing does.


According to Vertex’s Ken Crovetti and Scott Druckenmiller, the trust that makes that possible doesn’t come only from the product. It comes from being certified and visible on[SAP Store](https://store.sap.com/) .


## **Why “disjointed” is the enemy**


Druckenmiller, SAP partner channel sales manager at Vertex, describes the problem the partnership is built to solve: companies buying a stack of point solutions that don’t talk to each other. “Nobody wants to buy a point solution anymore,” Druckenmiller says. “Everybody wants to make sure all the dots connect.”

[Explore SAP Store](https://www.sap.com/store)


Vertex’s answer is to embed itself so deeply into SAP’s[order-to-cash](https://sap.com/products/financial-management/accounts-receivable.html) and procure-to-pay processes that the two systems function as one. Every order that runs through SAP triggers a tax calculation from Vertex at the same moment pricing is calculated, tied to the same master data—customers, products, vendors—that SAP already manages. Break that connection and orders stall. Keep it intact and you get what SAP calls a “no-touch order,” one that moves from creation to invoice to the general ledger without anyone stepping in.


Crovetti, business development lead for the SAP relationship at Vertex, frames the value in terms customers immediately understand: cash flow. Miscalculate tax, set aside too much or too little, and a company’s cash position takes the hit. “We want to keep that cash flow with you,” Crovetti says, “so you can grow, get bigger, better, faster, more efficient.”


## **Certification as the trust signal**


Crovetti works directly between Vertex’s sales organization and SAP’s—his job is to be a trusted advisor to joint customers. SAP Store is central to how he does that.


Druckenmiller frames the online marketplace as a filter for customers that are otherwise bombarded by vendors claiming SAP compatibility: “\[SAP\] Store is a great way for them to understand which ones are SAP blessed—and not just blessed, certified.” That[certification](https://sap.com/partners/partner-program/build.html) is what separates a claim from a guarantee.


Crovetti uses the word “matchmakers” to describe what SAP Store enables: connecting Vertex, SAP account teams, the customer, and sometimes a systems integrator around a shared need, before a formal sales process even begins. “\[SAP\] Store becomes that window to connect everybody,” he says.


Druckenmiller makes the prospect experience concrete with a simple analogy: “It’s no different than how we go online and look at buying a car. You know everything about your car before you walk into the dealership. We want to give our customers that same experience.” To that end, Vertex puts short demo videos on SAP Store—showing the tax engine running inside the SAP interface, not Vertex’s own UI—so a prospect can see what it looks like before committing to a full discovery cycle.


## **Part of the family**


Crovetti puts it plainly: once you’ve gone through SAP’s certification process and landed on[SAP Store](https://news.sap.com/tags/sap-store/) , “You’re part of the family.” That’s not just symbolic. It means SAP’s credibility transfers to partners who’ve earned it—and that the trust Vertex would otherwise have to build from scratch with every new prospect is already there when the conversation starts.


“\[SAP\] Store becomes not just a marketplace,” Druckenmiller says, “but an opportunity for customers to find certified solutions that can fill a gap”—whether that’s cloud ERP transformation, a compliance need, or something in between.


[Watch the video](https://youtu.be/JpirAnVM4EQ?si=OupRpUeY3uzWNpxp) to hear directly from Crovetti and Druckenmiller on how Vertex builds trust with SAP customers through certification, integration, and SAP Store.
